# Introduction

This document implements a complete preprocessing pipeline for single-cell RNA-seq data.
The pipeline can create Seurat objects from raw count matrices or AnnData .h5ad files;
the current analysis starts from compressed, tab-delimited raw UMI count matrices and
their corresponding cell annotation files. The workflow performs basic quality control
filtering based on mitochondrial gene expression and prepares the datasets for downstream
analyses such as normalization, clustering, and visualization.


# Libraries

```{r}
library(Matrix)
library(Seurat)
library(reticulate)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(DescTools)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
# library(ggvenn)
# library(pals)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggrepel)
library(Nebulosa)
library(scMRMA)

project_dir <- "/home/drighelli/lncRNA_project"

data_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "DATA")

# Reserved for possible AnnData (.h5ad) inputs.
datah_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "DATAH")

# Store all CRC-specific results separately from other outputs.
out_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "OUT", "CRC")

dir.create(
  out_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

source(file.path(project_dir, "functions.R"))
```

# Dataset definition

All datasets to be processed are defined in a single list.
Each entry contains three fields: `counts` is the path to a compressed, tab-delimited raw
UMI count matrix; `meta` is the path to the corresponding cell annotation file; and `save`
is the path where the resulting Seurat object is saved.

To add a new dataset, simply append a new GSE entry to this list.

```{r}
datasets <- list(
  
  GSE144735 = list(
    counts = file.path(data_dir, "GSE144735_processed_KUL3_CRC_10X_raw_UMI_count_matrix.txt.gz"),
    meta = file.path(data_dir, "GSE144735_processed_KUL3_CRC_10X_annotation.txt.gz"),
    save = file.path(out_dir, "obj_GSE144735_qc.rds")
  ),
  
  GSE132465 = list(
    counts = file.path(data_dir, "GSE132465_GEO_processed_CRC_10X_raw_UMI_count_matrix.txt.gz"),
    meta = file.path(data_dir, "GSE132465_GEO_processed_CRC_10X_cell_annotation.txt.gz"),
    save = file.path(out_dir, "obj_GSE132465_qc.rds")
  ),
  
  GSE132257 = list(
    counts = file.path(
      data_dir,
      "GSE132257_GEO_processed_protocol_and_fresh_frozen_raw_UMI_count_matrix.txt.gz"
    ),
    meta = file.path(
      data_dir,
      "GSE132257_processed_protocol_and_fresh_frozen_cell_annotation.txt.gz"
    ),
    save = file.path(out_dir, "obj_GSE132257_qc.rds")
  )
  
)

# To add a fourth dataset:
# simply add another element in the list above following the same structure.
```

# Preprocessing pipeline (loop over datasets)

This loop uses `load_txt_counts_to_seurat()` to process all datasets currently defined
above from raw UMI count matrices and cell annotation files, and stores the resulting
Seurat objects in a list.

```{r}
obj_list <- list()

for (name in names(datasets)) {
  
  cat("Processing dataset:", name, "\n")
  
  obj_list[[name]] <- load_txt_counts_to_seurat(
    counts_file = datasets[[name]]$counts,
    meta_file = datasets[[name]]$meta,
    save_path = datasets[[name]]$save
  )
  
  cat("Completed dataset:", name, "\n\n")
}

print(names(obj_list))

saveRDS(obj_list, file.path(out_dir, "obj_list_all.rds"))

obj_list[[1]]

```

# Merge Datasets

```{r}
merged_obj <- merge_seurat_objects(obj_list = obj_list, save_path = file.path(out_dir, "merged_seurat_qc.rds"))

# Check Merged objs

dim(merged_obj)

print(merged_obj)

table(merged_obj$GSE)

head(merged_obj@meta.data)

# Remove obj_list

rm(obj_list)
gc()
```

# QC Visualization

This section evaluates basic quality control metrics across datasets,
including number of detected genes, total counts, and mitochondrial percentage.

```{r}
merged_obj <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "merged_seurat_qc.rds"))
obj <- merged_obj

# define dataset colors (consistent palette)
cols <- scales::hue_pal()(length(unique(obj$GSE)))

VlnPlot(
  obj,
  features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
  group.by = "GSE",
  cols = cols,
  ncol = 3,
  pt.size = 0
)
```

# Dimensionality Reduction

This section performs normalization, feature selection, scaling,
PCA, and UMAP embedding for downstream visualization.

```{r}
obj <- NormalizeData(obj)

obj <- FindVariableFeatures(
  obj,
  selection.method = "vst",
  nfeatures = 2000
)

obj <- ScaleData(obj, features = VariableFeatures(obj))

obj <- RunPCA(obj, features = VariableFeatures(obj), npcs = 30)

ElbowPlot(obj)

obj <- RunUMAP(obj, dims = 1:15)
```


# Save Processed Object

Save the processed Seurat object after normalization and dimensionality reduction.

```{r}
saveRDS(obj, file.path(out_dir, "merged_normalized_hvgs.rds"))
# obj <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "merged_normalized_hvgs.rds"))
```


# UMAP Visualization


# Cell type specificity

This section quantifies cell type specificity of lncRNAs and protein-coding genes
using the Gini coefficient computed from DotPlot-based expression summaries.

```{r}
obj <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "merged_seurat_qc.rds"))

obj <- seurat_preprocess(obj)

gencode <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "gencode_v49_compatible.txt"), header = TRUE)

gene_sets <- gene_biotype_matching(obj, gencode)

lnc_features <- gene_sets$lnc
prot_features <- gene_sets$prot
ambiguous_genes <- gene_sets$ambiguous

chunk_size <- 2000

GiniCoef_lnc <- compute_gini_pipeline(obj, lnc_features, "lncRNA", chunk_size)
GiniCoef_prot <- compute_gini_pipeline(obj, prot_features, "protein_coding", chunk_size)

GiniCoef <- rbind(GiniCoef_lnc, GiniCoef_prot)
colnames(GiniCoef)[1] <- "gene"

saveRDS(GiniCoef, file.path(out_dir, "gini_dotplot_v49.rds"))

GiniCoef <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "gini_dotplot_v49.rds"))

GiniCoef_clean <- GiniCoef[!is.na(GiniCoef$gini), ]

lnc_n  <- nrow(GiniCoef_clean %>% filter(type == "lncRNA"))
prot_n <- nrow(GiniCoef_clean %>% filter(type == "protein_coding"))

plot_gini_results(GiniCoef_clean, lnc_n, prot_n)
```

# GRN Expression Filtering

## STEP 1: Calculate Expression Statistics

Objective:
- summarize gene expression across pseudobulk samples
- inspect the expression distribution
- support an informed choice of filtering thresholds

No genes are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_expression_qc <- calculate_grn_expression_statistics(
  expression_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_logcpm,
  count_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_counts
)

summary(grn_expression_qc$mean_logcpm)

summary(grn_expression_qc$median_logcpm)

summary(grn_expression_qc$n_detected_pseudobulk)
```

## STEP 2: Inspect Expression Distribution

Objective:

- visualize gene expression across pseudobulk samples
- identify genes with very low detection
- support the selection of filtering thresholds

No filtering is applied at this stage.

```{r}
grn_expression_plots <- plot_grn_expression_distribution(
  expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc
)

grn_expression_plots$mean_logcpm

grn_expression_plots$detected_pseudobulk
```

## STEP 3: Select Filtering Thresholds

Objective:

- define expression-based filtering criteria for GRN construction

The initial GRN analysis is performed without expression filtering.

Filtering thresholds will be defined after validating the unfiltered GRN
workflow and evaluating the impact of expression filtering on lncRNA
representation.

## STEP 4: Apply Expression Filtering

Objective:

- remove lowly expressed genes according to the selected thresholds

Expression filtering will be applied after validating the unfiltered GRN
workflow, allowing a direct comparison between filtered and unfiltered
networks.

# Spearman Correlation Analysis

## STEP 1: Prepare Unfiltered GRN Expression Matrix

Objective:

- restrict the normalized pseudobulk matrix to lncRNA and protein-coding genes
- preserve all GRN candidate genes before correlation analysis
- identify genes with zero variance across pseudobulk samples

No genes are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_correlation_input <- prepare_grn_correlation_matrix(
  expression_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_logcpm,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
)

dim(grn_correlation_input$expression)

length(grn_correlation_input$zero_variance_genes)

grn_correlation_input$n_genes

grn_correlation_input$n_samples
```

## STEP 2: Compute Unfiltered Spearman Correlations

Objective:

- compute pairwise Spearman correlations across all GRN candidate genes
- preserve the complete gene-gene correlation matrix
- establish the unfiltered baseline for downstream GRN construction

No correlation threshold is applied at this stage.

```{r}
grn_spearman_matrix <- compute_grn_spearman_correlations(
  expression_matrix = grn_correlation_input$expression
)

dim(grn_spearman_matrix)

sum(is.na(grn_spearman_matrix))

range(grn_spearman_matrix)

# saveRDS(grn_spearman_matrix, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_spearman_unfiltered.rds"))
```

# Correlation Network Filtering

## STEP 1: Inspect Correlation Strength Distribution

Objective:

- summarize pairwise Spearman correlations across GRN candidate genes
- quantify the number of gene pairs retained at different correlation strengths
- support an informed choice of correlation thresholds

No correlation filtering is applied at this stage.

```{r}
# grn_spearman_matrix <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_spearman_unfiltered.rds"))
grn_correlation_summary <- summarize_grn_correlations(
  correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix
)

grn_correlation_summary$summary

grn_correlation_summary$threshold_counts

grn_spearman_distribution_plot <- plot_grn_spearman_distribution(
  correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix
)

grn_spearman_distribution_plot
```

## STEP 2: Inspect Correlations by Gene-Pair Type

Objective:

- characterize correlations according to gene-pair type
- distinguish lncRNA-lncRNA, lncRNA-protein-coding, and protein-coding pairs
- evaluate lncRNA representation across different correlation strengths

No correlation filtering is applied at this stage.

```{r}
grn_correlation_by_type <- summarize_grn_correlations_by_gene_type(
  correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
)

grn_correlation_by_type
```

## STEP 3: Inspect Correlation Structure by Gene Detection

Objective:

- evaluate whether strong correlations are associated with low gene detection
- compare detection patterns across lncRNA and protein-coding genes
- assess whether highly correlated gene pairs are supported across pseudobulk samples

No genes or correlations are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_correlation_detection_summary <-
  summarize_grn_correlations_by_detection(
    correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix,
    expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc,
    gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
  )

grn_correlation_detection_summary
```

# GRN Expression Filtering - Finalization

The unfiltered GRN validation showed that the complete workflow preserves
lncRNA representation, but strong correlations are largely associated with
genes detected in very few pseudobulk samples.

The expression filtering workflow introduced previously is therefore completed
at this stage before final network inference.

## STEP 3: Select Filtering Thresholds

Objective:

- define expression-based filtering criteria based on the observed detection
  patterns
- reduce correlations driven by poorly detected genes
- preserve lncRNA representation for downstream GRN inference

```{r}
grn_detection_thresholds <- evaluate_grn_detection_thresholds(
  expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
)

grn_detection_thresholds

grn_detection_threshold_plots <- plot_grn_detection_thresholds(
  detection_thresholds = grn_detection_thresholds,
  selected_threshold = 2
)

grn_detection_threshold_plots$retained_counts

grn_detection_threshold_plots$retention_proportion
```

A minimum detection threshold of 2 pseudobulk samples was selected for the
CRC dataset.

This conservative threshold removes genes that are never detected or detected
in only one pseudobulk sample, which were found to strongly contribute to the
high correlations observed in the unfiltered CRC analysis.

The selected threshold retains 3,223 lncRNA genes, preserving substantial
lncRNA representation for downstream CRC GRN inference.

## STEP 4: Apply Expression Filtering

Objective:

- remove genes that do not satisfy the selected expression criteria
- generate the filtered expression matrix used for final GRN inference
- retain the unfiltered analysis as a baseline for comparison

```{r}
grn_filtered <- apply_grn_expression_filter(
  expression_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_logcpm,
  count_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_counts,
  expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets,
  min_detected_pseudobulk = 2
)

dim(grn_filtered$expression)

length(grn_filtered$gene_sets$lnc)

length(grn_filtered$gene_sets$prot)

length(grn_filtered$retained_genes)

length(grn_filtered$removed_genes)

saveRDS(grn_filtered, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_filtered.rds"))
# grn_filtered <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_filtered.rds"))
```

# GENIE3 Network Inference

## STEP 1: Prepare Candidate Regulators

Objective:

- identify human transcription factors supported by the curated Human TF database
- restrict candidate regulators to protein-coding genes retained after CRC expression filtering
- prepare a biologically informed regulator set for GENIE3 inference

```{r}
human_tf <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "DatabaseExtract_v_1.01.txt"), header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

grn_genie3_regulators <- prepare_genie3_regulators(
  human_tf = human_tf,
  filtered_gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets,
  expression_matrix = grn_filtered$expression
)

length(grn_genie3_regulators)

head(grn_genie3_regulators)
```

## STEP 2: Configure GENIE3 Inference

Objective:

- define reproducible GENIE3 inference parameters
- use curated transcription factors as candidate regulators
- retain all filtered GRN genes as potential targets

```{r}
grn_genie3_config <- list(
  tree_method = "RF",
  K = "sqrt",
  n_trees = 1000,
  n_cores = 8
)

grn_genie3_config
```

## STEP 3: Run GENIE3 Network Inference

Objective:

- infer directed regulatory relationships from filtered pseudobulk expression
- use curated transcription factors as candidate regulators
- retain all filtered genes as potential targets
- compute GENIE3 importance scores using Random Forests

```{r}
set.seed(grn_config$random_seed)

grn_genie3_weights <- GENIE3::GENIE3(
  exprMatrix = as.matrix(grn_filtered$expression),
  regulators = grn_genie3_regulators,
  treeMethod = grn_genie3_config$tree_method,
  K = grn_genie3_config$K,
  nTrees = grn_genie3_config$n_trees,
  nCores = grn_genie3_config$n_cores
)

saveRDS(grn_genie3_weights, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_genie3_weights.rds"))

dim(grn_genie3_weights)
sum(is.na(grn_genie3_weights))
range(grn_genie3_weights)
```

# Spearman and GENIE3 Integration

## STEP 1: Integrate GENIE3 and Spearman Results

Objective:

- combine GENIE3 importance scores with Spearman correlations
- associate each candidate TF-target interaction with its expression correlation
- retain the direction of regulation inferred by GENIE3 and the sign of the corresponding Spearman correlation
- prepare candidate regulatory interactions for GRN construction

```{r}
grn_genie3_weights <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_genie3_weights.rds"))
grn_integrated_edges <- integrate_genie3_spearman(
  genie3_weights = grn_genie3_weights,
  spearman_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix
)

dim(grn_integrated_edges)

head(grn_integrated_edges)

summary(grn_integrated_edges$genie3_weight)

summary(grn_integrated_edges$spearman_rho)

sum(is.na(grn_integrated_edges))
```

## STEP 2: Inspect Integrated Edge Score Distributions

Objective:

- characterize the distribution of GENIE3 importance scores
- evaluate the strength of Spearman correlations among candidate interactions
- assess the effect of different score thresholds on network size
- support an informed selection of criteria for GRN construction

No interactions are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_integrated_summary <- summarize_grn_integrated_edges(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges
)

grn_integrated_summary$genie3_summary

grn_integrated_summary$spearman_summary

grn_integrated_summary$genie3_quantiles

grn_integrated_summary$threshold_counts

grn_genie3_importance_plot <- plot_grn_genie3_importance_distribution(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges
)

grn_genie3_importance_plot

grn_threshold_selection_plot <- plot_grn_threshold_selection(
  threshold_counts = grn_integrated_summary$threshold_counts,
  selected_genie3_quantile = 0.995,
  selected_spearman_threshold = 0.5
)

grn_threshold_selection_plot
```

## STEP 3: Evaluate Candidate Network Composition

Objective:

- evaluate network composition across candidate GENIE3 and Spearman thresholds
- quantify lncRNA representation in candidate networks
- compare network size with preservation of biologically relevant targets
- support the final selection of GRN construction criteria

No final network threshold is selected at this stage.

```{r}
grn_candidate_networks <- evaluate_grn_candidate_networks(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges,
  filtered_gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets,
  genie3_quantile_table = grn_integrated_summary$genie3_quantiles
)

grn_candidate_networks

grn_lnc_retention_plot <- plot_grn_lnc_retention_vs_network_size(
  candidate_networks = grn_candidate_networks,
  selected_genie3_quantile = 0.995,
  selected_spearman_threshold = 0.5
)

grn_lnc_retention_plot
```

## STEP 4: Evaluate lncRNA Edge Representation

Objective:

- quantify regulatory interactions targeting lncRNA and protein-coding genes
- compare lncRNA edge representation across selected candidate networks
- verify that candidate thresholds preserve substantial lncRNA connectivity
- support the final selection of GRN construction criteria

No final network is constructed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_candidate_settings <- data.frame(
  genie3_quantile = c(0.99, 0.995),
  genie3_cutoff = c(0.008532776, 0.011259691),
  spearman_threshold = c(0.5, 0.5)
)

grn_lnc_edge_representation <- evaluate_grn_lnc_edge_representation(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges,
  filtered_gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets,
  candidate_settings = grn_candidate_settings
)

grn_lnc_edge_representation
```

# GRN Construction

## STEP 1: Construct Final GRN

Objective:

- apply the selected GENIE3 and Spearman criteria
- retain high-confidence TF-target regulatory interactions
- preserve GENIE3 importance and Spearman correlation as edge attributes
- generate the final CRC GRN edge list for downstream network analysis

```{r}
grn_final_edges <- construct_final_grn(
```

# Integrated lncRNA-TF-PCG Regulatory Network

## STEP 1: Prepare Integrated GRN Gene Sets

Objective:

- reuse the genes already retained by the previous GRN expression-filtering step
- define three gene classes for the integrated network:
  - lncRNA
  - transcription factors (TF)
  - protein-coding genes excluding TFs
- ensure that all selected genes are represented in the filtered pseudobulk expression matrix
- verify that the three gene classes are mutually exclusive

These gene sets will be reused as regulator and target groups in the subsequent
GENIE3 analyses.

The previous GRN filtering strategy is preserved unchanged.

```{r}
integrated_lnc <- intersect(grn_filtered$gene_sets$lnc, rownames(grn_filtered$expression))

integrated_tf <- intersect(grn_genie3_regulators, rownames(grn_filtered$expression))

integrated_pcg <- setdiff(grn_filtered$gene_sets$prot, integrated_tf)
integrated_pcg <- intersect(integrated_pcg, rownames(grn_filtered$expression))

integrated_grn_gene_sets <- list(
  lncRNA = integrated_lnc,
  TF = integrated_tf,
  PCG = integrated_pcg
)

length(integrated_grn_gene_sets$lncRNA)
length(integrated_grn_gene_sets$TF)
length(integrated_grn_gene_sets$PCG)

length(intersect(integrated_grn_gene_sets$lncRNA, integrated_grn_gene_sets$TF))
length(intersect(integrated_grn_gene_sets$lncRNA, integrated_grn_gene_sets$PCG))
length(intersect(integrated_grn_gene_sets$TF, integrated_grn_gene_sets$PCG))

all(c(
  integrated_grn_gene_sets$lncRNA,
  integrated_grn_gene_sets$TF,
  integrated_grn_gene_sets$PCG
) %in% rownames(grn_filtered$expression))

saveRDS(integrated_grn_gene_sets, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_gene_sets.rds"))
# integrated_grn_gene_sets <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_gene_sets.rds"))

```

## STEP 2: Infer TF-to-PCG Interactions

Objective:

- infer putative regulatory interactions from transcription factors to
  protein-coding target genes
- use the filtered pseudobulk expression matrix defined in the previous GRN
  workflow
- use GENIE3 to estimate directional regulator-target importance scores
- integrate each GENIE3 interaction with the corresponding Spearman correlation
- annotate the resulting interactions as TF-to-PCG

This step uses the general regulator-target inference procedure that will also
be reused for the other interaction classes of the integrated GRN.

No final GENIE3 or Spearman threshold is applied at this stage.`

```{r}
integrated_tf_pcg <- infer_integrated_grn_relationships(
  expression_matrix = grn_filtered$expression,
  spearman_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix,
  regulators = integrated_grn_gene_sets$TF,
  targets = integrated_grn_gene_sets$PCG,
  regulator_type = "TF",
  target_type = "PCG",
  edge_type = "TF_to_PCG",
  seed = grn_config$random_seed,
  n_cores = 4
)

dim(integrated_tf_pcg$weights)
dim(integrated_tf_pcg$edges)

head(integrated_tf_pcg$edges)

table(integrated_tf_pcg$edges$edge_type)

saveRDS(integrated_tf_pcg, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_tf_pcg.rds"))
# integrated_tf_pcg <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_tf_pcg.rds"))
```

## STEP 3: Infer TF-to-lncRNA Interactions

Objective:

- infer putative regulatory interactions from transcription factors to lncRNA targets
- reuse the same GENIE3 and Spearman integration procedure applied to TF-to-PCG interactions
- use the filtered TF and lncRNA gene sets defined for the integrated GRN
- annotate the resulting interactions as TF-to-lncRNA

GENIE3 provides model-based regulator-to-target directionality, while Spearman
correlation provides complementary association support across pseudobulk samples.

No final GENIE3 or Spearman threshold is applied at this stage.

```{r}

  edge_type = "TF_to_lncRNA",
  seed = grn_config$random_seed,
  n_cores = 4
)
```

## STEP 6: Inspect Interaction Class Score Distributions

Objective:

- inspect GENIE3 importance score distributions separately for each interaction class
- inspect signed and absolute Spearman correlation distributions
- calculate GENIE3 and Spearman quantiles for each interaction class
- compare score distributions before applying any final network filter
- retain the four interaction classes separately during threshold evaluation

The four GENIE3 runs are inspected independently because their importance-score
distributions may differ according to regulator and target set composition.

No edges are removed at this step.

To limit memory usage, interaction classes are loaded and inspected sequentially
rather than simultaneously.

```{r}
# TF → PCG

integrated_tf_pcg <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_tf_pcg.rds"))

tf_pcg_score_distribution <- inspect_integrated_grn_score_distribution(
  edges = integrated_tf_pcg$edges,
  edge_type = "TF_to_PCG"
)

tf_pcg_score_distribution$summary
tf_pcg_score_distribution$genie3_quantiles
tf_pcg_score_distribution$spearman_quantiles
tf_pcg_score_distribution$abs_spearman_quantiles

rm(integrated_tf_pcg)
gc()
```


### Save Interaction Class Score Distribution Summary

The score-distribution results obtained independently for the four interaction
classes are collected and saved for downstream filtering.

The combined summary reports the number of candidate edges, zero GENIE3 weights,
and missing GENIE3 or Spearman values for each interaction class.

The complete distribution object additionally preserves the GENIE3, signed
Spearman, and absolute Spearman quantiles calculated for each class.

These results provide the reference distributions that will be used in the next
step to define class-specific filtering thresholds before network integration.

No interaction is filtered or removed at this stage.

```{r}
integrated_score_distribution_summary <- rbind(
  tf_pcg_score_distribution$summary,
  tf_lnc_score_distribution$summary,
  lnc_pcg_score_distribution$summary,
  lnc_tf_score_distribution$summary
)

integrated_score_distribution_summary

integrated_score_distributions <- list(
  TF_to_PCG = tf_pcg_score_distribution,
  TF_to_lncRNA = tf_lnc_score_distribution,
  lncRNA_to_PCG = lnc_pcg_score_distribution,
  lncRNA_to_TF = lnc_tf_score_distribution
)

saveRDS(integrated_score_distributions, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_score_distributions.rds"))

write.table(
  integrated_score_distribution_summary,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_score_distribution_summary.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## STEP 7: Filter Individual Interaction Classes

Objective:

- evaluate alternative filtering thresholds for the four interaction classes
- define GENIE3 thresholds independently from each interaction-class distribution
- combine relative GENIE3 importance with absolute Spearman correlation support
- quantify the number and proportion of retained interactions under alternative filtering scenarios
- select a filtering criterion before integrating the four interaction classes

Because GENIE3 importance-score distributions differ across interaction classes,
GENIE3 thresholds are defined using class-specific quantiles rather than a single
absolute importance cutoff.

Spearman correlation is evaluated using its absolute value so that both positive
and negative associations can provide support for an inferred interaction.

Filtering is performed independently for each interaction class before network
integration.

### STEP 7A: Evaluate Candidate Filtering Thresholds

Several combinations of GENIE3 quantiles and absolute Spearman correlation
thresholds are evaluated before selecting the final filtering criterion.

This sensitivity analysis reports the number and proportion of interactions that
would be retained in each interaction class without modifying the original
interaction tables.

```{r}
# TF → PCG

integrated_tf_pcg <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_tf_pcg.rds"))

tf_pcg_filter_evaluation <- evaluate_integrated_grn_filter_thresholds(
  edges = integrated_tf_pcg$edges,
  edge_type = "TF_to_PCG"
)

tf_pcg_filter_evaluation

rm(integrated_tf_pcg)
gc()
```

```{r}
# TF → lncRNA

integrated_tf_lnc <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_tf_lnc.rds"))

tf_lnc_filter_evaluation <- evaluate_integrated_grn_filter_thresholds(
  edges = integrated_tf_lnc$edges,
  edge_type = "TF_to_lncRNA"
)

tf_lnc_filter_evaluation

rm(integrated_tf_lnc)
gc()
```

```{r}
# lncRNA → PCG

integrated_lnc_pcg <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_lnc_pcg.rds"))

lnc_pcg_filter_evaluation <- evaluate_integrated_grn_filter_thresholds(
  edges = integrated_lnc_pcg$edges,
  edge_type = "lncRNA_to_PCG"
)

lnc_pcg_filter_evaluation

rm(integrated_lnc_pcg)
gc()
```

```{r}
# lncRNA → TF

integrated_lnc_tf <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_lnc_tf.rds"))

lnc_tf_filter_evaluation <- evaluate_integrated_grn_filter_thresholds(
  edges = integrated_lnc_tf$edges,
  edge_type = "lncRNA_to_TF"
)

lnc_tf_filter_evaluation

rm(integrated_lnc_tf)
gc()
```

### Combine and Save Filtering Threshold Evaluation

The filtering evaluations obtained independently for the four interaction classes
are combined into a single summary table.

The resulting table reports, for each interaction class and each tested threshold
combination, the class-specific GENIE3 cutoff, the absolute Spearman correlation
threshold, and the number and fraction of retained interactions.

These results are saved for comparison and will be used to select the final
filtering criterion before generating the filtered interaction classes.

No final filtering is applied at this stage.

```{r}
integrated_filter_evaluation <- rbind(
  tf_pcg_filter_evaluation,
  tf_lnc_filter_evaluation,
  lnc_pcg_filter_evaluation,
  lnc_tf_filter_evaluation
)

integrated_filter_evaluation

saveRDS(integrated_filter_evaluation, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_filter_evaluation.rds"))

write.table(
  integrated_filter_evaluation,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_filter_evaluation.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

### STEP 7B: Apply Selected Filtering Criteria

Based on the threshold sensitivity analysis, the final filtering criterion is
applied independently to each interaction class.

For each class, interactions are retained when:

- the GENIE3 importance score is at or above the 95th percentile of the
  corresponding interaction-class distribution
- the absolute Spearman correlation is at least 0.5

Using class-specific GENIE3 quantiles accounts for differences in importance-score
distributions across the four GENIE3 runs, while the Spearman threshold provides
additional expression-based support for the inferred relationships.

The four filtered interaction classes are kept separate and saved independently.
Their integration into a single regulatory network is performed in the next step.

```{r}
# User-defined filtering parameters: adjust the GENIE3 quantile and
# absolute Spearman correlation threshold to select the desired filtering stringency.

integrated_genie3_quantile <- 0.95
integrated_spearman_threshold <- 0.5
```

```{r}
# TF → PCG

integrated_tf_pcg <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_tf_pcg.rds"))

filtered_tf_pcg <- filter_integrated_grn_relationships(
  edges = integrated_tf_pcg$edges,
  genie3_quantile = integrated_genie3_quantile,
  spearman_threshold = integrated_spearman_threshold
)

filtered_tf_pcg$summary
dim(filtered_tf_pcg$edges)

saveRDS(filtered_tf_pcg, file.path(grn_out_dir, "filtered_tf_pcg.rds"))

rm(integrated_tf_pcg)
gc()
```

```{r}
)

filtered_tf_lnc$summary
dim(filtered_tf_lnc$edges)
```

### Summarize and Save Filtered Interaction Classes

The filtering summaries from the four interaction classes are combined to verify
the number and proportion of interactions retained by the selected criterion.

Only filtering metadata are combined at this stage. The filtered interaction
tables remain separate and will be merged into the integrated regulatory network
in the next step.

```{r}
integrated_filter_summary <- rbind(
  filtered_tf_pcg$summary,
  filtered_tf_lnc$summary,
  filtered_lnc_pcg$summary,
  filtered_lnc_tf$summary
)

integrated_filter_summary

sum(integrated_filter_summary$retained_edges)

write.table(
  integrated_filter_summary,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_filter_summary.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(integrated_filter_summary, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_filter_summary.rds"))
```

## STEP 8: Integrate Filtered Interaction Classes

Objective:

- combine the four independently filtered interaction classes into a single integrated regulatory network
- preserve GENIE3, Spearman, regulator-type, target-type, and interaction-class annotations
- verify that no required edge information is missing after integration
- identify the complete set of nodes represented in the integrated network
- assign each node to one of the three gene classes: lncRNA, TF, or PCG
- verify the consistency of node-type assignments before downstream annotation and network analysis

Only interactions retained by the class-specific filtering procedure are integrated.

No additional biological or visualization filter is applied at this step. 

```{r}
filtered_tf_pcg <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "filtered_tf_pcg.rds"))
filtered_tf_lnc <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "filtered_tf_lnc.rds"))
filtered_lnc_pcg <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "filtered_lnc_pcg.rds"))
filtered_lnc_tf <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "filtered_lnc_tf.rds"))

integrated_grn_gene_sets <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_gene_sets.rds"))

filtered_interaction_classes <- list(
  TF_to_PCG = filtered_tf_pcg$edges,
  TF_to_lncRNA = filtered_tf_lnc$edges,
  lncRNA_to_PCG = filtered_lnc_pcg$edges,
  lncRNA_to_TF = filtered_lnc_tf$edges
)

integrated_grn <- integrate_filtered_grn_interaction_classes(
  edge_tables = filtered_interaction_classes,
  gene_sets = integrated_grn_gene_sets
)

dim(integrated_grn$edges)
dim(integrated_grn$nodes)

integrated_grn$summary

table(integrated_grn$edges$edge_type)

table(integrated_grn$nodes$node_type, useNA = "ifany")

table(
  integrated_grn$edges$regulator_type,
  integrated_grn$edges$target_type
)

head(integrated_grn$edges)
head(integrated_grn$nodes)

sum(is.na(integrated_grn$nodes$node_type))

saveRDS(integrated_grn, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn.rds"))

write.table(
  integrated_grn$edges,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_grn_edges.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.table(
  integrated_grn$nodes,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_grn_nodes.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.table(
  integrated_grn$summary,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_grn_integration_summary.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

rm(
  filtered_tf_pcg,
  filtered_tf_lnc,
  filtered_lnc_pcg,
  filtered_lnc_tf,
  filtered_interaction_classes
)

gc()
```

## STEP 9: Annotate lncRNA-Target Interactions with LncTarD

Objective:

- annotate lncRNA-to-PCG and lncRNA-to-TF interactions in the integrated GRN using LncTarD
- preserve all interactions already retained by the GRN filtering procedure
- identify exact directed lncRNA-target pairs reported in LncTarD
- distinguish database-supported interactions from data-driven candidate interactions
- record the number of LncTarD entries supporting each GRN interaction
- preserve the corresponding LncTarD record identifiers for downstream interpretation

LncTarD is used only as an external annotation resource and does not determine
which interactions are retained in the integrated GRN.

Matching is performed on the directed regulator-target pair. Therefore, a
LncTarD interaction supports a GRN edge only when both regulator and target
match in the same direction.

Interactions not reported in LncTarD are retained in the network and remain
putative data-driven candidates.

```{r}
integrated_grn <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn.rds"))

lnctard_file <- file.path(data_dir, "lnctard2.0.txt")

lnctard <- read.delim(
  lnctard_file,
  header = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE,
  quote = ""
)

lnctard$Regulator <- iconv(lnctard$Regulator, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
lnctard$Target <- iconv(lnctard$Target, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")

dim(lnctard)

lnctard_annotation <- annotate_integrated_grn_with_lnctard(
  integrated_edges = integrated_grn$edges,
  lnctard = lnctard
)

lnctard_annotation$summary

dim(lnctard_annotation$edges)
dim(lnctard_annotation$lnc_edges)
dim(lnctard_annotation$supported_edges)

table(
  lnctard_annotation$lnc_edges$edge_type,
  lnctard_annotation$lnc_edges$lnctard_supported
)

head(lnctard_annotation$supported_edges)

integrated_grn$edges <- lnctard_annotation$edges

saveRDS(integrated_grn, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_lnctard_annotated.rds"))

saveRDS(
  lnctard_annotation,
  file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_lnctard_annotation.rds")
)

write.table(
  lnctard_annotation$summary,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_grn_lnctard_summary.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.table(
  lnctard_annotation$supported_edges,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "integrated_grn_lnctard_supported_edges.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## STEP 10: Analyze Integrated GRN Structure, Motifs and Cascades

Objective:

- characterize the global structure of the filtered and integrated GRN
- quantify nodes and directed edges by gene and interaction class
- calculate network degree statistics and identify highly connected nodes
- distinguish positive and negative associations according to the Spearman correlation
- quantify LncTarD-supported interactions in the final network
- summarize major two-step lncRNA-TF-PCG regulatory cascades without materializing all global paths
- construct a reusable directed graph representation of the complete integrated GRN
- prepare the network for whole-network visualization and gene-centered path exploration

The network is analyzed without applying additional filtering.

Global cascade analysis reports the number of compatible directed two-step paths
without enumerating every individual path, avoiding unnecessary expansion of the
complete network.

The complete directed graph is preserved for downstream analysis. Individual
paths are therefore explored on demand for a selected gene, direction, and
maximum depth in STEP 12 rather than being globally enumerated.

Global network visualization is performed in STEP 11.

## STEP 11: Visualize the Integrated GRN

Objective:

- visualize the complete filtered and integrated GRN
- include all retained nodes and directed edges without additional visualization filtering
- distinguish lncRNA, TF, and PCG nodes
- distinguish the four regulatory interaction classes
- preserve the complete network structure generated in the previous steps
- save a reusable network layout and the complete GRN visualization for downstream inspection

The visualization includes the complete integrated network and does not select
top nodes, hubs, or interaction subsets for graphical convenience.

Because the network contains a large number of nodes and edges, a layered
representation is used to separate lncRNA, TF, and PCG nodes into distinct
regions of the plotting space.

Edge transparency and reduced graphical width are used only to limit overplotting.
No nodes or edges are removed from the network.

Node labels are omitted from the global plot because displaying more than
18,000 labels would obscure the overall network structure.

The complete network is visualized here, while gene-specific labeled subnetworks
and user-defined neighborhood depth are explored separately in STEP 12.

```{r}
dir.create(file.path(grn_out_dir, "plots"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

integrated_grn_graph <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_graph.rds"))

igraph::vcount(integrated_grn_graph)
igraph::ecount(integrated_grn_graph)
igraph::is_directed(integrated_grn_graph)

table(igraph::vertex_attr(integrated_grn_graph, "node_type"))

table(igraph::edge_attr(integrated_grn_graph, "edge_type"))

integrated_grn_plot <- plot_integrated_grn(
  graph = integrated_grn_graph,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  vertex_size = 0.8,
  edge_width = 0.08,
  edge_alpha = 0.04,
  arrow_size = 0
)

saveRDS(integrated_grn_plot$layout, file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_layout.rds"))

png(
  filename = file.path(grn_out_dir, "plots", "integrated_grn_complete_layered.png"),
  width = 6000,
  height = 3000,
  res = 300
)

plot_integrated_grn(
  graph = integrated_grn_graph,
  layout = integrated_grn_plot$layout,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  vertex_size = 0.8,
  edge_width = 0.08,
  edge_alpha = 0.04,
  arrow_size = 0
)

dev.off()

file.exists(file.path(grn_out_dir, "plots", "integrated_grn_complete_layered.png"))

file.info(
  file.path(grn_out_dir, "plots", "integrated_grn_complete_layered.png")
)$size
```

## STEP 12: Explore Selected Gene Neighborhood and Depth - CASC19

Objective:

- explore the integrated GRN starting from a user-selected gene
- analyze incoming, outgoing, or bidirectional network neighborhoods
- control the maximum exploration depth
- quantify nodes reached at each minimum network distance from the selected gene
- distinguish the complete induced neighborhood from the depth-layer network
- retrieve the complete gene-centered subnetwork within the selected depth
- retrieve edges connecting consecutive exploration levels
- enumerate directed simple paths from the selected gene when requested
- preserve GENIE3, Spearman, interaction-class, node-type, and LncTarD annotations
- visualize the depth-layer gene-centered network

The exploration is performed on the complete filtered integrated GRN without
applying additional biological filtering.

The selected gene, direction, and maximum depth are user-defined parameters.

Two complementary network representations are retained:

- the induced subnetwork contains all interactions occurring among the nodes
  reached within the selected depth
- the layer network contains only interactions connecting consecutive minimum
  distance levels relative to the selected gene

The layer network is used for depth-oriented visualization, while the complete
induced subnetwork remains available for additional network analysis.

Neighborhood exploration and path enumeration are treated separately because
the number of possible simple paths can increase rapidly with network depth.

CASC19 is used as the initial example, but the same workflow can be applied to
any gene represented in the integrated GRN.

```{r}
integrated_grn_graph <- readRDS(
  file.path(grn_out_dir, "integrated_grn_graph.rds")
)

# User-defined gene exploration parameters.
selected_gene <- "CASC19"
selected_direction <- "out"
selected_depth <- 1
enumerate_gene_paths <- TRUE
maximum_paths <- 100000

# User-defined visualization parameters.
# Use NULL to display all interaction classes.
# Example:
# selected_edge_types <- "lncRNA_to_TF"
# selected_edge_types <- c("lncRNA_to_TF", "TF_to_PCG")
selected_edge_types <- "lncRNA_to_TF"

gene_exploration <- explore_integrated_grn_gene(
  graph = integrated_grn_graph,
  gene = selected_gene,
  direction = selected_direction,
  depth = selected_depth,
  enumerate_paths = enumerate_gene_paths,
  max_paths = maximum_paths
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Numerical summaries
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

gene_exploration$summary

gene_exploration$depth_summary

gene_exploration$node_type_summary

# Complete induced-subnetwork edge composition.
gene_exploration$edge_type_summary

# Depth-layer edge composition.
gene_exploration$layer_edge_type_summary

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inspect reached nodes and edges
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

dim(gene_exploration$nodes)

dim(gene_exploration$edges)

dim(gene_exploration$layer_edges)

head(gene_exploration$nodes)

# All edges among nodes reached within the selected depth.
head(gene_exploration$edges)

# Only edges connecting consecutive depth levels.
head(gene_exploration$layer_edges)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inspect simple paths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (!is.null(gene_exploration$paths)) {
  dim(gene_exploration$paths)
  head(gene_exploration$paths, 20)
}

gene_exploration$paths_truncated

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize the depth-layer network
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

gene_exploration_plot <- plot_integrated_grn_gene_neighborhood(
  exploration = gene_exploration,
  show_labels = TRUE,
  edge_types_to_show = selected_edge_types
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save complete exploration object
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  gene_exploration,
  file.path(
    grn_out_dir,
    paste0(
      "integrated_grn_",
      selected_gene,
      "_",
      selected_direction,
      "_depth",
      selected_depth,
      ".rds"
    )
  )
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Export summary
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

write.table(
  gene_exploration$summary,
  file = file.path(
    grn_out_dir,
    "tables",
    paste0(
      "integrated_grn_",
      selected_gene,
      "_",
      selected_direction,
      "_depth",
      selected_depth,
      "_summary.tsv"
    )
  ),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Export reached nodes
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

write.table(
  gene_exploration$nodes,
  file = file.path(
    grn_out_dir,
    "tables",
    paste0(
      "integrated_grn_",
      selected_gene,
      "_",
      selected_direction,
      "_depth",
      selected_depth,
      "_nodes.tsv"
    )
  ),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Export complete induced-subnetwork edges
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

write.table(
  gene_exploration$edges,
  file = file.path(
    grn_out_dir,
    "tables",
    paste0(
      "integrated_grn_",
      selected_gene,
      "_",
      selected_direction,
      "_depth",
      selected_depth,
      "_induced_edges.tsv"
    )
  ),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Export depth-layer edges
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

write.table(
  gene_exploration$layer_edges,
  file = file.path(
    grn_out_dir,
    "tables",
    paste0(
      "integrated_grn_",
      selected_gene,
      "_",
      selected_direction,
      "_depth",
      selected_depth,
      "_layer_edges.tsv"
    )
  ),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Export simple paths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (!is.null(gene_exploration$paths)) {
  write.table(
    gene_exploration$paths,
    file = file.path(
      grn_out_dir,
      "tables",
      paste0(
        "integrated_grn_",
        selected_gene,
        "_",
        selected_direction,
        "_depth",
        selected_depth,
        "_paths.tsv"
      )
    ),
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```
